subject: Webhook endpoints failing with 504 Gateway Timeout
customer_email: Hi team, our webhook subscriber for 'ticket.created' events has been failing with 504 Gateway Timeout since 2 PM today. Are your webhook payloads experiencing retry loops or sending oversized bodies? - Alex Chen, Tech Lead
intent: Webhook delivering 504 gateway timeout on ticket.created events
ground_truth_reply:
Hi Alex,

Thanks for reaching out with these technical details.

Our webhook dispatch servers enforce a strict 5-second HTTP timeout for subscriber acknowledgement (HTTP 200 OK). When your endpoint takes longer than 5 seconds to respond, our gateway terminates the connection with a 504 status and enqueues the event for exponential backoff retry.

To resolve this, we recommend:
1. Having your receiving server return an immediate HTTP 200/202 upon payload receipt.
2. Offloading heavy downstream processing (such as CRM synchronizations or database writes) to an asynchronous worker queue (e.g., Celery, SQS, or Redis Queue).

Our payload sizes have remained constant (~4 KB). You can review delivery attempt logs and manual redelivery options under Settings > Integrations > Webhooks > Delivery Logs.

Best regards,
Developer Support Team
key_facts: Webhook timeout threshold is 5 seconds
Requires immediate HTTP 200/202 before processing payload
Recommend asynchronous queue for downstream processing
Logs available in Settings > Integrations > Webhooks > Delivery Logs
prohibited_actions: Do not promise to increase server timeout beyond system limits
Do not claim webhook server is down without verifying gateway metrics

To resolve this in your Okta Admin Console:
1. Go to Applications > Your App > General tab > SAML Settings > Edit.
2. In the 'Audience URI (SP Entity ID)' field, ensure the value is exactly: `https://app.ourdomain.com/sso/saml/{your_subdomain}` (without trailing slash).
3. Ensure the 'Recipient' and 'Destination' URLs match `https://app.ourdomain.com/sso/saml/acs`.
4. Save changes and test SSO in an incognito window.

In the meantime, Account Admins can still authenticate using email and password via `https://app.ourdomain.com/login?fallback=direct`. Let us know if you need us to join a screen share to review your SAML attributes.

Best regards,
Enterprise Support Team

Hi Samantha,

Using dynamic placeholders is a great way to personalize replies while saving your team time!

We support the following dynamic placeholders in all shared email templates:
- `{{contact.first_name}}` - Recipient's first name (e.g., Samantha)
- `{{contact.last_name}}` - Recipient's last name
- `{{ticket.id}}` - Unique ticket reference number (e.g., #TK-1029)
- `{{agent.first_name}}` - The sending agent's first name
- `{{company.name}}` - Customer company name

To create a template with placeholders:
1. Navigate to Settings > Shared Templates > 'Create New Template'.
2. While composing, click the **'Insert Placeholder' ({{ }})** icon in the rich text toolbar or type the placeholder directly.
3. Provide a fallback value (e.g., `{{contact.first_name | 'there'}}`) in case a contact record lacks a first name.
4. Click 'Save & Share with Team'.

When your agents insert the template into a reply, our system automatically populates the exact contact and ticket values. Let us know if you need any help creating your first set!

Best regards,
Customer Support Team

subject: Difference between Member, Admin, and Guest roles
customer_email: Hi, we are setting up our organization permissions. What is the difference between an Admin, a Member, and a Guest in shared mailboxes? Who can see customer billing info? - Jason Kuo

1. **Admin / Owner**:
   - Full system access.
   - Manage subscription, billing, and credit cards.
   - Add/remove users and create/delete shared mailboxes.
   - Configure global automation rules and SLA policies.

2. **Member**:
   - Daily operational agent.
   - Can view, assign, reply to, and tag conversations in assigned shared mailboxes.

   - Can view conversations and leave internal notes.

   - No billing access.

Only users with the **Admin** or **Account Owner** role can see or manage billing information. You can configure role assignments under Settings > Team Management > Users.

Best regards,
Customer Support Team

subject: How to set up automated CSAT survey after ticket resolution

intent: How to configure automated Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) survey upon ticket closure
ground_truth_reply:
Hi Jordan,

Tracking CSAT is one of the best ways to keep a pulse on customer sentiment, and setting it up takes just a few clicks!

Here is how to enable automated CSAT surveys:
1. Navigate to Settings > Customer Feedback & CSAT.
2. Click 'Enable CSAT Surveys' and select your shared mailbox.
3. Choose your survey trigger: 'Send automatically when conversation status changes to Closed'.
4. (Recommended) Set a survey cooldown delay (e.g., send 15 minutes after closing) to prevent sending surveys if an issue is quickly reopened.
5. Customize your rating scale (1-5 stars or 2-point Good/Bad) and thank-you message.
6. Click 'Save & Activate'.

You can review aggregate CSAT trends and agent scorecards in your Analytics > CSAT Reports tab. Let us know if you need any assistance customizing your survey template!

Best regards,
Customer Support Team

Analytics > CSAT Reports tab for metrics

6. Complete the one-time SMTP verification to allow your agents to reply directly using `support@domain.com` as the sender.

This setup is 100% free of extra Google licensing fees. Full documentation is available here: `docs.ourdomain.com/setup/google-alias`.

Customer Support Team

Technical Support Team

subject: Accidental email send to wrong customer containing sensitive contract details
customer_email: URGENT ESCALATION: One of our junior reps accidentally replied to Ticket #91823 and included an attachment meant for a different client containing proprietary contract terms. The email was sent 2 minutes ago. Can your system recall or unsend this message? - Victor Sullivan, General Counsel
intent: Emergency recall request for sensitive email sent to incorrect recipient
ground_truth_reply:
Dear Victor,

I understand the critical urgency and confidentiality of this situation.

Here is the immediate status and actions taken:

1. **Undo Send Window Check**:
   - If the sending agent is within the 30-second 'Undo Send' window configured in Gmail or our interface, they must click the 'Undo' notification banner immediately at the bottom of their screen.
2. **External Delivery Reality**:
   - Once an email has passed the Undo window and traversed external SMTP servers to the recipient's mail host, internet email protocol (SMTP) does not permit an external sender to force-delete an email from an external recipient's inbox.
3. **Immediate Mitigation Steps**:
   - If the attachment was sent as a secure cloud link (Google Drive/Dropbox/DocuSign), immediately revoke public permissions or delete the file from your cloud drive to prevent access.
   - We can assist in drafting an immediate formal recall/confidentiality notice to the recipient requesting deletion in accordance with non-disclosure standards.
   - I have placed an administrative lock on ticket #91823 to preserve all access logs for your compliance and legal review.

Please let us know if the attachment was linked via cloud drive or if you would like our team to assist with an incident log export.

Sincerely,
Executive Incident Response & Security Support
key_facts: Explain 30-second Undo Send window
Honest technical disclosure: SMTP cannot forcibly delete delivered external mail
Mitigation: revoke cloud file permissions immediately
Administrative lock placed on ticket to preserve legal audit logs
prohibited_actions: Never falsely promise that an external SMTP email has been recalled when impossible
Do not panic the customer, provide actionable mitigation steps
